recipes.name: Authentic Mexican Corn Bread
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) can sweetened condensed milk (such as La Lechera®)
2 (15.25 ounce) cans whole kernel corn, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 2-quart baking dish.
Whisk sweetened condensed milk and sugar together in a large bowl. Whisk in eggs, and vanilla. Stir in whole kernel corn, cream-style corn, and butter.
Whisk cornmeal, flour, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; stir cornmeal mixture into the corn mixture.
Pour batter into the prepared baking dish.
Bake until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cornbread comes out clean, about 45 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Authentic Mexican Corn Bread
raw_recipe.description: This sweet Mexican cornbread uses two kinds of corn, condensed milk, and cornmeal to make a rich, sweet cornbread that's more like a spoon bread.

review.reviewBody: I made this but used 2 cans of cream corn and 1 1/2 cups of fresh sweet corn and it was amazing.

I didn't have 2 cans of regular corn so I winged it and added 4oz or so of heavy cream. (Yes, I know.) Also skipped the sugar because my condensed milk was sweetened. Baked it in a pre-heated iron skillet. Best cornbread ever.
I tried the recipe...it was delicious and decadent. However, I recommend a 9x13x2 inch baking dish. A 2 quart baking dish is much too small. The 9x13x2 is perfect.

wow, this recipe is decadent! I used two cans of cream corn like others suggested. it turned out rich and fluffy and moist and absolutely delicious. but this is definitely a treat rather than an everyday recipe.

notes: use a 3 quart baking dish (I used 9x13) rather than the 2 quart dish the recipe called for. it makes sooooo much. I cut mine into 32 pieces! also, watch the baking time. mine only needed 40 minutes.

if I make this again I will definitely try to lighten it up a bit. I'll stick to one can creamed corn and add the milk like others suggested. it doesn't need the optional sugar and 1/4 cup butter would be plenty. might omit an egg or two as well. finally, I'll add the diced green chilis I was planning on adding this time around but forgot. bah!

I made this cornbread following others reviews I used 1 can corn and 2 cans cream style corn, but did make muffins and cooked them for 15-18 minutes, I made some with diced green chilies and some without I used some cupcake liners and some without , but all three batches came out good, it made 36 muffins with me filling the muffin tins with 1/3 cup of batter and it goes great with the slow cooker chicken taco soup on this site...will make these again =D

This is wonderful. We have to make it dairy-free due to food allergies, so we used 2 small cans of Cream of Coconut in place of the sweetened condensed milk, and Earth Balance in place of the butter, though we have used coconut oil with great results. We do not add the extra sugar, because we feel like it's sweet enough with the coconut cream. We also modify with one can of corn and 2 cans of cream-style corn. Very moist and rich, perfect for serving with soup. Sweet, with a good depth to it. I even ate it for breakfast a few mornings!

Per other suggestions, I used 2 cans of creamed corn and fresh chopped jalapeños (mine were not spicy but added texture and flavor). I used defrosted frozen corn bcs that’s what I had but I bet it would have been fine to leave it out if needed. I also did not use the optional sugar. I may try it next time for a sweet bread but it wasn’t missed. Very moist.

Awesome! I added jalapeño and shredded cheddar cheese, and omitted vanilla. I didn’t add the optional sugar but next time I’ll put it in because I think it’ll make it even better! Also per other reviews I used 2 cans cream corn with 1 can regular corn.

This recipe is AMAZING. Very moist and so delicious! I added 3 diced jalapenos to the recipe to give it a little spice and it was really great! 

Note: There's no way the recipe fits in a 2-qt baking dish; you have to use a 3-qt dish.

After reading some of the reviews, I decided to use some sugar, but only 1/4 cup. Also didn't want the bread too moist but not dry so I used half cup of Milk. Finally added mild jalapeno peppers for a bite. I used mild cause of my kiddos. If this was just for myself and husband I would of added hot peppers. Baked it in my cast iron skillet for 45 minutes and it was perfect! Yum!

Omg this was so good! I read the reviews and decided to add 1 cup of vitamin D milk JIC it is dry. I probably didnt need to do that but still no regrets. I also used real butter at room temp so maybe that helped? I added fresh jalapenos on one side of the pan, I have kids, and im so pleased with how moist it turned out, sweet and authentic flavors. Its not so sweet like cake but pretty close to it! The jalepenos really do compliment it!
I added 1 tsp of baking powder to lighten it up. Also some chipotle peppers and it was great 👍

Followed as written but added green chili's and some dried red peppers. Skipped optional sugar and was happy with level of sweetness. Next time I'll use blender to make whole kernel corn less noticeable. May try again with mexicorn. Thanks for nice recipe.
Flavor Good Large quantity Heavy and texture dense
Delicious! I followed other reviews and used 2 cans cream of corn and 1 can corn. I also added a small can of diced jalapeños to give it some kick!
I made this exactly as the recipe instructed. Needs to be baked longer for the middle to get done. Cover it so if doesn't brown too much. Very very sweet but very good with a spicy meal.
Delicious!!!! Love this recipe
This is delicious, love this recipe!
I make this all the time as is. it's very moist and delicious. to help it cook better and faster I make them into muffins. huge success.
I often 'tweak' recipes for my own taste, but this one looked good right out of the box and it is! It's a really nice moist corn bread that goes perfect with soup.
